[Rating: 1/10] Has a neat concept, cannibalise your starting resources (ships) to build the hubs of your space station.  Unfortunately there isn't much else.  The central concept could be the guts of an interesting 12-15 turn / 30-45 minute game, where you have to judge exactly when to dismember your engine but Space Station Phoenix in its current low interaction version drags on and on (2+ hours) with the same repetitive actions.  It's an interesting miss.  A different take on cannibalising your engine is The Bloody Inn which is better.

[Rating: 1/10] Salvaging engines sounded kinda cute in theory. But in the end it's just about building alternate engines.

[Rating: 2/10] Read the rules and some warnings started going off in my head. Taught the game and everyone started saying "where's the rest of the game?". Painfully shallow and monotonous. Slowly collect resources. Dump them to build a section of your space station and not care which one it is because it has relatively little impact. Fill it with aliens. Rinse. Repeat. Bored as hell. The board is too open at the start and while you slowly tear down the various action spaces over the course of the game, it is of almost no consequence as players collect income to free up the action spaces much more frequently.

[Rating: 3/10] This reflects a 4p playthrough. I expect some of the more glaring issues to be diminished on lower counts. The game starts out great but quickly devolves into a repetitive task of doing the same actions and income over and over for a very long period of time. About halfway through I wanted it to be over. Although there is variety on Hubs and Sectors, the actions are only 5 and they are not particularly exciting ones either. I didn't have a single exciting moment where I pull off a good move or my engine starts popping off. Also, diplomacy is more of a chore to remember every single opponent's 

[Rating: 3/10] It sounded good on paper, but turned out to be incredibly dull.  Probably most similar to Space Gate Odyssey, although I feel it wanted to be Race For The Galaxy or something similar.  Way too much setup and way too long for what it is.  Combos are too few and too weak, engine building is too slow and too weak, the decisions you make aren't interesting enough.  Probably the most unique thing in the game is the action space deconstruction, but that just doesn't make up for the rest.  I would rather play a lot of other similar games including Space Gate Odyssey over this.

[Rating: 3/10] The mechanics would be fine (if unremarkable) in a 60 minute game, but Space Station Phoenix is much too simple and repetitive to justify the nearly 3 hours it ended up lasting in the 4 player game I played. I would actively avoid playing it again solely because of the length.

[Rating: 3/10] This game have one mistake. People play only one way to win by dyplomacy - collect VP. And all other method is invalid. So this game is imperfect.

[Rating: 3/10] Space Station Phoenix is simply not my cup of tea. The game overstays its welcome with monotonous, uneventful turns, in which you procure an incremental resource advantage to use several turns later. A majority of your end game points are dictated by your starting hub and residence majorities, for which you may have minimal agency, depending on what other players receive/pursue.
